question: Switch the paper's feature-count ladder (A_fi app:rh_fi_ladder, fig:rh_ladder, tab:rh_channels_sparse Panel B, the introduction and conclusion sentences) from the monthly ladder to the every-bar one (addendum K, not pre-registered), as C4 provisionally set? If so: the forest has no every-bar ladder (keep its monthly row labelled, or drop it); the window x k grid (app:rh_fi_scaling) exists only monthly (keep it monthly and labelled, or move it); Panel B moves to the every-bar ordinary / statement-day spans.

solvers.answer: Switch. Drop the forest from the every-bar figure and Panel B and keep its monthly result as one labelled appendix clause; keep the grid monthly and labelled; Panel B on the every-bar day-type spans; the not-pre-registered label goes in appendix prose, not in the caption.

Switch. Keep the forest's monthly ladder as a dashed line in the figure and a marked row in Panel B; grid monthly and labelled; no pre-registration label in caption or note, disclosure in the 'Added after the rule' list of A_results and in A_fi.

Switch. Drop the forest from the figure and Panel B, one labelled appendix sentence; grid monthly and labelled; the figure caption and the Panel B note say the every-bar version is not pre-registered.

refutation.note: Majority answer (switch; forest out of Panel B and the figure with one labelled monthly sentence; no pre-registration label in the caption or the note; grid monthly and labelled) checked against the repo. (1) The author's words: transcript bd4224e0 2026-10-29T00:02:27Z (agent's recommendation, including 'Random forest: ... I'd leave it monthly and label it so') and 00:04:29Z 'go'; 2026-10-29T00:20:59Z (labels 'get rid of this') and 00:30:03Z ('for the stray line break and other notes, yes'), applied in commit c872c53 ('the order of the analyses stays in the appendix'); A1; 29 Oct 14:23 'did we update the ladder tables on overleaf?'. No later author message on the ladder (last typed message 14:32 PDT, skill call 14:42), and log.jsonl has no veto of C4 (Q-2026-10-29-05, provisional). (2) Numbers: ladall_readings.csv and ladall_scores.csv match the EB macros (linear R10 115/105/104, k90 10 in all five, trees R10 97/96); ladall_checks.json passes. (3) Forest: its monthly Panel B Full cells are -44.4 (statement days) and -4.6 (ordinary days), sparsity table line 35, against -44.8 and -5.3 in the joint row of tab:rh_channels_abl (lines 29, 42): keeping the row would recreate for the forest the mismatch the switch removes for the other five (lasso ordinary days +1.0 against -2.4). 'Label it so' is met by the labelled sentence and by the caption and note saying the forest is refitted only monthly; tab:rh_ablation_beyond already prints 'the random forest is not run' in the main text. The author-record solver's dagger precedent marks pre-patch cells within one refit design, a weaker analogue. (4) Labels: addendum K (h) asks that every output carry the label, but it is agent-written; the author's later-dated words of 28 Oct 17:20/17:30 removed the same labels from three table notes (PROTOCOL section 5 rule 2), and the generated files' header comments keep it. (5) Grid: rehaul_complexity_numbers.tex header shows the patched fomcfix grid, so A_fi.tex:496 'The design precedes the FOMC-calendar patch' is stale; an every-bar grid or forest would be unapproved compute. (6) Where-used: paper_rehaul.tex:175 inputs only the monthly macro file, and the beat layers and the fresh version also use the monthly ladder macros; the every-bar caption self-references fig:rh_ladder. No lock or forbid found against the switch. The majority answer survives.

precedence_note: The switch: D1 (25 Oct, every bar), the 28 Oct 16:58-17:04 messages and 'go', and A1 (28 Oct 23:22) all point the same way; no author decision favours the monthly ladder. Labels: the author's 28 Oct 17:20/17:30 removal of 'requested by the author ... not part of the pre-specified design' from table notes governs captions and notes and outranks the agent-written addendum K (h) (section 5 rule 2); the order of the analyses stays in the appendix prose. C4 (inferred, T2) composes and keeps its separate 16:00 figure. D16 keeps the 16:00 bar out of the main text.
final_answer: Yes: switch. The paper's feature-count ladder is the every-bar ladder of addendum K wherever it is reported: the text of app:rh_fi_ladder, fig:rh_ladder, Panel B of tab:rh_channels_sparse, and the introduction and conclusion sentences (their wording is Q-2026-10-29-31). The pre-specified monthly ladder stays, labelled monthly, only where the every-bar run has no counterpart: the dashed lines of the figure, one sentence on the random forest, the 16:00 figure that C4 moves to app:rh_closing, and the window x k grid. Nothing is refitted or rescored. (1) Random forest: not in the every-bar figure or in Panel B; its monthly result is one labelled sentence in the trees bullet of app:rh_fi_ladder (wording in Q-2026-10-29-31), and the figure caption and the Panel B note say it is refitted only monthly. No every-bar forest run. (2) Labels: no 'requested by the author' or 'not pre-registered' in the figure caption or the Panel B note. The order of the analyses is stated in appendix prose: a new 'Order of the analyses' item in app:rh_fi_ladder and a new item in the 'Added after the rule' list of A_results.tex. The generated files' header comments keep addendum K's label. (3) Window x k grid: stays monthly, labelled 'the monthly version of the feature-count ladder'; the stale pre-patch sentence is deleted. (4) Panel B: the every-bar statement-day and ordinary-day spans, five rows, so its Full column equals the joint row of tab:rh_channels_abl. (5) The every-bar figure takes the label fig:rh_ladder; the monthly figure is relabelled fig:rh_ladder_monthly and is the source of C4's 16:00 figure only. No 16:00 span is scored on the every-bar forecasts. Replacement text and generator changes are in actions[].detail; one commit for the item, then the routine Overleaf push.
answer_short: Your ladder is now the every-bar one (figure, Panel B, intro, conclusion); the monthly ladder stays, labelled, for the forest, the 16:00 bar and the window grid.
rationale: All three lenses switch, for the same checked reasons: the monthly Panel B contradicts the main-text table printed above it (lasso ordinary days +1.0 against -2.4), the monthly shares are not shares of Table 1's gain, and the author asked for the every-bar rerun and for every-bar results wherever they back a claim (A1). The two minority positions were resolved with checked reasons: the forest's monthly row would recreate the mismatch the switch removes, and the caption label goes against the author's 28 Oct removal of the same labels. Confidence 0.75: the switch about 0.9, the forest handling about 0.7, the label placement about 0.85. T2 (majority agreement, confidence below 0.8, no hard trigger). HIGH: a main-text table, the introduction and conclusion, and the refit design of a reported result. Consequence 4.

l.369: \input{generated/rehaul_ladder_fig_everybar} replaces \input{generated/rehaul_ladder_fig}. l.371-383 (the first item's design text, up to its sub-list; the sub-list items are replaced under Q-2026-10-29-31) become:
\item \textbf{How many series carry the gain} (Figure~\ref{fig:rh_ladder}). Following
  \citet{MaischZhangUlrichZimmer2026}, we refit each model on its top $k$ exogenous series only, $k = 1$, 3, 5, 10
  and 20, re-estimated at every bar as in Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos} (window of \rhldEBWindowDays{} trading days, frozen
  hyperparameters); $k = 0$ (the HAR benchmark set) and $k = \rhldEBNSeries$ (the full set) are the forecasts of
  Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos}. Every rung is scored on the \rhldEBNBars{} bars of Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos}, and on the
  \rhldEBNDaysOrd{} ordinary days and the \rhldEBNDaysEv{} FOMC statement days of Section~\ref{sec:rh_fi}. Each model
  ranks the series once, by its own measure on a fit explained on \rhldEBRankYear, before the span, so the ranking
  has no look-ahead. Rung $k$ retains $R_k = (L_0 - L_k)/(L_0 - L_{\rhldEBNSeries})$ of the full set's QLIKE gain. A
  model's signal reads concentrated if \rhldRuleKConc{} or fewer series retain \rhldRulePct\% of the gain,
  intermediate if 10 or 20 are needed, and dense and weak if no reduced rung reaches \rhldRulePct\%. The figure and
  the numbers below, like the same ladder by day type in Panel~B of Table~\ref{tab:rh_channels_sparse}, cover
  LightGBM, XGBoost, ridge, lasso and elastic net on the design with the FOMC fixes of
  Appendix~\ref{app:rh_dp_fomc}.
After the closing paragraph (current l.410-414, replaced under Q-2026-10-29-31) and before \end{itemize}, add a second top-level item:
\item \textbf{Order of the analyses.} The pre-specified ladder refitted each rung at the \rhldNOrigins{} monthly
  origins of Appendix~\ref{app:rh_fi_compute} and held each fit for \rhldHoldSessions{} sessions; its rungs, rankings
  and reading were fixed before it was scored. Held for a month, the full sets are less accurate than those of
  Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos}, by \rhldPctMonthlyVsWalkMin{} to \rhldPctMonthlyVsWalkMax\%, so its shares are not shares of
  Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos}'s gain. Refitting every rung at every bar was added after that comparison and is not part of
  the pre-specified design; its design was fixed in a dated addendum before its forecasts were made, and it is read
  with the pre-specified rule. Figure~\ref{fig:rh_ladder} draws the monthly rungs dashed. The random forest has only
  the monthly ladder.
